What does each image contribute?

How to interpret these measurements

FEATURE DETECTION PRECEDES MATCHING

These counts are the number of stored SIFT keypoint rows in each image. They describe detected image features; they are not matched pairs or unique 3D points. Multiple images can detect the same scene detail. More detected features can help matching, but blur, repeated textures, weak overlap, and moving objects still affect reconstruction.

Mean and median summarize each resolution. The distribution shows whether many images have few useful features or whether a small number of richly textured frames dominate the mean. Keeping frame IDs aligned lets you compare the same recorded view at different resolutions.

This notebook reads only the new manual GUI trial databases. Earlier automated reconstructions remain documented in Step 1. Empty databases and images without a stored feature record are marked pending rather than treated as zero.
